$comment: W1.6 licence policy: ONE policy over the npm lockfiles, the browser bundle (licenceModules() in vite.config.ts),
platform-engine/engines.lock.json and the data assets (fonts, ICC profiles). Enforced by scripts/licence-check.mjs
(CI step 'Licence gate' in .github/workflows/ci.yml); notices by scripts/notices.mjs. Licences are SPDX ids.
Browser bundle: MIT, Apache, BSD, ISC, MPL and OFL only. GPL/LGPL: server-only and only from serverCopyleft.
Blocked everywhere: AGPL, SSPL, BUSL, PolyForm, CC-NC, source-available and no-licence code.
A violation found in today's dependencies is never fixed here by changing a dependency: it goes under
'exceptions' as an owner decision with a reason, so CI stays green and the decision stays visible on every run.

browser.$comment: Families: MIT (MIT, MIT-0), Apache (Apache-2.0), BSD (BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, 0BSD), ISC, MPL (MPL-2.0), OFL (OFL-1.1).

server.$comment: Backend image, Workers, the engine image and dev tooling (dev tools use the server rules). The browser list plus other permissive licences with notice-only duties.

blocked.reason: Sustainable Use License: source-available (fair-code), commercial distribution restricted

copyleft.$comment: GPL and LGPL (any version, with or without exceptions such as the font exception). Never in the browser; on the server only for the names below. Names are npm package names, 'engine:<id>' for engines.lock.json entries and 'asset:<name>' for data assets.

serverAllowlist.reason: libvips (LGPL-3.0-or-later) through sharp: prebuilt shared library, server-only, unmodified
sharp's Windows build bundles libvips (LGPL-3.0-or-later); dev machines only
sharp's WebAssembly build bundles libvips (LGPL-3.0-or-later); never loaded in the browser
libvips in the engine image (LGPL), dynamically linked
poppler-utils in the heavy pool, run as a separate process on our own output (GPL)
ffmpeg as a separate process (LGPL/GPL build), server-only

denyPackages.reason: Tiptap Pro: paid, not open source
the original pdf-lib is unmaintained; use the maintained @cantoo/pdf-lib fork

elections.$comment: Dual-licensed packages and the option we use. The elected licence must be one of the OR alternatives.

jszip.reason: jszip is (MIT OR GPL-3.0-or-later); we use it under its MIT option

clarifications.$comment: Lockfile licence strings that are not SPDX, mapped after reading the package's licence file. Keyed by name@version so an update is re-read.

duck@0.1.12.evidence: package.json says 'BSD'; node_modules/duck/LICENSE is the 2-clause BSD text (Copyright (c) 2013, Michael Williamson)

@codesandbox/nodebox@0.1.8.evidence: package.json says 'SEE LICENSE IN ./LICENSE'; node_modules/@codesandbox/nodebox/LICENSE is the Sustainable Use License 1.0 (licensor CodeSandBox B.V.): internal or non-commercial use only, free non-commercial distribution only

exceptions.reason: Source-available code in the browser bundle. Pulled in by @codesandbox/sandpack-client <- @codesandbox/sandpack-react (Apache-2.0), the chat code playground (components/chat/ReactPlayground.tsx, MultiFilePlayground.tsx, artifacts/LiveComponentSandbox.tsx), and bundled into the lazy vendor-sandpack chunk that every visitor can download. The Sustainable Use License allows internal or non-commercial use and free non-commercial distribution only. Owner options: alias the Node runtime out of the bundle (only Node templates use it), replace the playground runtime, or accept the risk in writing.

W3C polyfill pulled in by @react-hook/intersection-observer <- @codesandbox/sandpack-react (chat code playground, lazy vendor-sandpack chunk). The W3C Software and Document License is permissive (notice only) but not on the browser list (MIT/Apache/BSD/ISC/MPL/OFL). Owner options: add W3C-20150513 to the browser list, or drop it together with the playground.

$lockfiles: The lockfiles below are always read; every other package-lock.json under the app (outside node_modules, build output and test fixtures) is found and read too, with the server rules unless its packages are in the browser bundle.

vendored.$comment: Third-party code copied into the repo. Every directory directly under a folder named 'vendor' needs a record here and must keep its licence file and a PATCHES.md next to the code.

engines.$lockfiles: The lockfiles below are always read; every other package-lock.json under the app (outside node_modules, build output and test fixtures) is found and read too, with the server rules unless its packages are in the browser bundle.
engines.$comment: Every engine binary that enters the platform-engine image: pinned by sha256, with its licence and source URL. Evaluated with the server rules under the name 'engine:<id>'. The schema is a JSON Schema subset (type, const, enum, required, properties, additionalProperties, items, pattern, minLength, maxLength, maxItems).

dataAssets.$comment: Every font and ICC profile file in the repo (outside node_modules and build output) must match exactly one record with its licence, its terms (what we may do with it) and the licence text file. Scope browser = served to browsers; server = backend image; engine = platform-engine image; qa = the QA harness build (dist-qa), checked with the browser rules.

customLicences.$comment: LicenseRef-* terms a data asset may carry (an ICC profile's licence, say), keyed by id: { terms, licenceText, scopes, verified }. 'verified' becomes true only after a human read the licence text; until then any record using it fails.
